Cluster_1.name: Cluster_1 (11 items) - Example: Centralised MCP Hub Architecture

items.title: Centralised MCP Hub Architecture
items.content: To centralise Model Context Protocol (MCP) management on macOS, shift from a Tool-Managed architecture (where each LLM client instantiates its own subprocesses) to a Service-Oriented architecture. Instead of subprocesses, establish a persistent 'MCP Host' or 'Gateway' that exposes tools via a unified interface, treating MCP servers as standalone daemons.

items.title: Centralisation via Local Proxy/Gateway
items.content:
One way to centralise MCP runtimes is using a gateway that provides a single entry point via a local SSE (Server-Sent Events) bridge. 
1. Host via PM2 or Launchd: Run MCP servers as background processes.
2. Expose via SSE: Use an SSE Bridge to convert Stdio-based servers into HTTP/SSE endpoints.
3. Unified Client Config: Point LLM clients to the same local URL instead of individual shell commands.

items.title: Symbolic Link Synchronisation for MCP Configs
items.content:
If tools must spawn their own processes, centralise the logic using symbolic links:
- Define a Master Config: Create `mcp-master.json` in `~/.config/mcp/`.
- Symlink Configs: `ln -s ~/.config/mcp/master.json ~/Library/Application\ Support/Antigravity/config.json` and `ln -s ~/.config/mcp/master.json ~/.config/gemini-cli/config.json`.
Outcome: Modifying one config updates all tools, though processes remain separate.

items.title: The MCP-Proxy Router Framework
items.content: Implement a thin MCP Proxy (Router) in Python or Node.js to manage downstream MCPs. The LLM client connects only to this Proxy via Stdio. The Proxy then manages the lifecycle of multiple internal MCPs (Filesystem, GitHub, Database, etc.).

items.title: Docker MCP Gateway (Native Hub)
items.content: The Docker MCP Gateway moves process management to the Docker daemon. Docker Desktop (v4.40+) includes a native MCP Toolkit and Gateway that aggregates tools into a single endpoint accessible via `docker mcp gateway run`.

items.title: Setting up Centralised MCP Hub on Colima
items.content:
To run a central MCP hub on Colima:
1. Start Colima: `colima start`.
2. Link Socket: `sudo ln -sf ~/.colima/default/docker.sock /var/run/docker.sock`.
3. Use Docker Compose with `docker/mcp-gateway:latest`, mapping `${HOME}/.colima/default/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock` and exposing port `8811` with `--transport=sse`.

items.title: Docker Compose Configuration for MCP Hub
items.content:
Example `docker-compose.yml` for an MCP Hub:
yaml
services:
  mcp-gateway:
    image: docker/mcp-gateway:latest
    container_name: mcp-hub
    environment:
      - DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock
    volumes:
      - ${HOME}/.colima/default/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - ./config:/root/.config/docker-mcp
    ports:
      - "8811:8811"
    command:
      - --servers=filesystem,github,memory
      - --transport=sse
      - --port=8811
    restart: always

items.title: Connecting Gemini CLI to Centralised MCP Hub
Implementing an MCP Router with Docker Compose
items.content:
Configure a gateway in router mode to manage many tools efficiently:
yaml
services:
  mcp-router:
    image: docker/mcp-gateway:latest
    command:
      - --mode=router
      - --default-servers=memory,filesystem
    ports:
      - "8811:8811"
  mcp-memory:
    image: mcp/memory:latest
    volumes:
      - ./data/memory.db:/app/data/memory.db
  mcp-filesystem:
    image: mcp/filesystem:latest

items.title: Optimizing IDE LLM Architecture
items.content:
Architectural Framework: Decoupling State from Compute

To solve "context rot"... you must shift your mental model of the IDE LLM.

- **Compute Layer (The IDE LLM):** Handles logic, code generation, and reasoning.
- **State Layer (Pieces LTM):** Handles persistence, temporal grounding, and context retrieval.
- **Interface Layer (MCP):** The Model Context Protocol acts as the API gateway.

items.title: Connecting Antigravity IDE to Centralised MCP Hub
Comparison of /sse vs /mcp Endpoints
items.content:
- `/sse` (Server-Sent Events): The classic two-channel transport. Opens a long-lived GET stream; client POSTs messages to unique session URLs. High compatibility with 'Remote MCP' tools.
- `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP): Modern, unified HTTP stream for bi-directional communication. More robust for high-concurrency and less resource-intensive than legacy SSE.

items.title: The 100-Tool Limit and Attention Dilution in LLMs
items.content:
The 100-tool warning in IDEs like Antigravity stems from technical bottlenecks:
1. Token Overhead: Every tool schema is injected into the System Prompt, consuming thousands of tokens.
2. Attention Dilution: Probability of 'Tool Hallucination' increases as the choice space expands. Models show reasoning dips when choosing between >50-80 complex tools.

items.title: The Router Pattern for MCP Tool Limits
items.content: To bypass tool limits, use a Router/Proxy pattern. The LLM sees only 'Meta-Tools' (e.g., `tool_search`, `tool_exec`). The Gateway hides low-level tools until specifically requested, dynamically providing schemas at the moment of need. This reduces context bloat and maintains model reasoning performance.

items.title: Bounded Context - Execution (Generic Subdomain)
items.content:
#### 3.3. Execution Context (Generic Subdomain)

Handles the asynchronous running of jobs.

- **Entities:** `Job`, `JobExecutionInfo`.
- **Role:** decoupling the "Definition" from the "Result". The UI polls this context for status.

items.title: OHDSI Atlas & WebAPI Domain Analysis - Executive Summary
items.content:
### 1. Executive Summary

This document provides a Domain-Driven Design (DDD) analysis of the OHDSI ecosystem, specifically focusing on the relationship between **Atlas** (Frontend/Bounded Context Consumer) and **WebAPI** (Backend/Domain Layer).

The system is architected around the core concept of **Cohort Definitions**—computable phenotypes—which serve as the Foundational Aggregate for all downstream analytics (Characterization, Estimation, Prediction).

items.title: Ubiquitous Language - Core Entities
items.content:
### 2. Ubiquitous Language The following terms constitute the **Ubiquitous Language** shared between the Code (Entities), the UI (Atlas), and the Domain Experts (Researchers). #### Core Entities | Term | Definition | Key Code Artifacts | |:--- |:--- |:--- | | **Cohort Definition** | The specification of criteria (rules) that define a group of persons for a specific duration. This is the **Aggregate Root**. | `CohortDefinition.java` (WebAPI)
`CohortDefinition.js` (Atlas) | | **Cohort** | The _instantiated_ result of applied criteria. A list of subjects with start/end dates. | `Cohort` (SQL Table)
`CohortGenerationInfo` | | **Source** | A specific database instance conforming to the OMOP Common Data Model (CDM) against which definitions are executed. | `Source` entity
`source_id` | | **Concept Set** | A collection of standard terminological concepts (SNOMED, RxNorm, etc.) used as building blocks for criteria. | `ConceptSet.js`
`CommonConceptSetEntity` | | **Generation** | The asynchronous _process_ of executing a Definition against a Source to materialize a Cohort. | `Job` (Batched execution)
`GenerationStatus` | | **Expression** | The JSON-serialized representation of the Cohort rules. This acts as the "Code as Data" for the phenotype. | `expression` (Field)
`CohortExpression` |

items.title: Ubiquitous Language - Analytic Contexts
items.content:
#### Analytic Contexts

| Term | Definition |
|:--- |:--- |
| **Characterization** | Descriptive statistics (demographics, conditions, drugs) describing a Cohort. |
| **Pathway** | Analysis of the temporal sequence of events (e.g., lines of therapy) within a Cohort. |
| **Estimation** | _Population Level Estimation_. Comparative effectiveness research (Cohort Method, Self-Controlled Case Series). |
| **Prediction** | _Patient Level Prediction_. Machine learning models to predict outcomes within a Cohort. |
| **Incidence Rate** | Analysis of the rate at which an outcome occurs within a target population. |

items.title: Bounded Context - Cohort Definition (Core Domain)
items.content:
#### 3.1. Cohort Definition Context (Core Domain)

This is the heart of the system.

- **Aggregate Root:** `CohortDefinition`
- **Entities:** `CohortDefinitionDetails` (holds the Expression), `CohortGenerationInfo` (State).
- **Value Objects:** `Expression` (The logic), `ConceptSet`.
- **Invariants:** A Definition must have a valid Expression. A Name must be unique.

items.title: Bounded Context - Vocabulary (Supporting Domain)
items.content:
#### 3.2. Vocabulary Context (Supporting Domain)

Handles the complex medical terminology.

- **Entities:** `Concept`, `Vocabulary`, `Domain`.
- **Role:** Provides the "Language" (`ConceptIds`) used inside the `Expression`.

items.title: Bounded Context - Analytic Subdomains
items.content:
#### 3.4. Analytic Subdomains

Each of these consumes `Cohort Definitions` to produce specific scientific outputs.

- **Characterization Context**
- **Estimation Context**
- **Prediction Context**

items.title: System Architecture - Atlas vs. WebAPI
items.content:
### 4. Architecture: Atlas vs. WebAPI

- **WebAPI (The Domain Layer):** Enforces the invariants. Encapsulates the OHDSI standard libraries (Circe for cohorts, SqlRender for translation). It exposes the Domain Model via a RESTful API.
- **Atlas (The Presentation Layer):** A "Smart Client" that speaks the Ubiquitous Language. It constructs the `Expression` object (via a UI builder) and sends it to the generic `CohortDefinition` aggregate in WebAPI.

items.title: Domain Model Diagram (D2)
items.content:
### 5. Domain Model Diagram

d2
# Core Aggregate
CohortDefinition: {
  "+Integer id"
  "+String name"
  "+String description"
  "+ExpressionType type"
  "+generate(Source)"
}

CohortDefinitionDetails: {
  "+String rules_json"
  "+getExpression()"
}

CohortGenerationInfo: {
  "+Integer source_id"
  "+GenerationStatus status"
  "+Date startTime"
  "+Long personCount"
}

Source: {
  "+String sourceKey"
  "+String sourceName"
  "+String cdmJdbcUrl"
}

# Relationships
CohortDefinition -- CohortDefinitionDetails: contains
CohortDefinition -- CohortGenerationInfo: tracks status for
CohortGenerationInfo -> Source: executes on

# Analytic Consumers
CohortCharacterization: {
  "+String name"
  "+List<CohortDefinition> cohorts"
}

PathwayAnalysis: {
  "+String name"
  "+List<CohortDefinition> targetCohorts"
  "+List<CohortDefinition> eventCohorts"
}

CohortCharacterization -> CohortDefinition: analyzes
PathwayAnalysis -> CohortDefinition: uses

items.title: Key Insight - The Expression/Specification Pattern
items.content:
#### Key Insight: The "Expression" Pattern

The system relies heavily on the **Specification Pattern**. The `CohortDefinition` doesn't contain hardcoded logic; it contains a serialized `Expression` (the Specification) which is interpreted by the engine (Circe/SqlRender) to generate SQL. This allows the Domain Logic to be dynamic and user-defined.
